title: Principal Neighbourhood Aggregation for Graph Nets
layout_note: Four states on one horizontal line joined by three long labelled arrows; the first state is itself a small hub-and-spoke (six neighbours arrowing into a centre node).
grouping: No containers, panels or frames: grouping is by position and colour alone. Each stage is a cluster of circles separated from the next by a long black arrow whose operation name sits above it (multiple aggregators, scalers, MLP) and, for the first two, whose options are listed in a square bracket below it (mean / max / min / std; identity / amplification / attenuation). Colour families: salmon for the neighbours, teal for the centre node and the output node, lavender for the aggregated copies, and lavender, red and blue for the three scaled stacks.
shapes_depth: Every object is a flat filled circle with a darker outline of its own hue (dark red around salmon, dark slate around teal, dark navy around lavender and blue, bright red around the red stack); no boxes, shadows or 3-D. Multiplicity is drawn as diagonally offset stacks of overlapping circles: four lavender circles after the aggregators, three stacks of four (lavender, red, blue) after the scalers. Neighbour-to-centre arrows are short dark slate arrows; stage arrows are long thin black arrows. Labels are plain sans above the arrows; the bracketed option lists are italic math-style words.
proposed_highlight: Nothing is boxed or named as a module; the method's operations exist only as arrow labels with their option lists in brackets. What carries the idea is colour and count: the single teal node becomes a stack of lavender copies, which splits into three differently coloured stacks, and an MLP returns a single node in the original teal.
lesson: Draw multiplicity instead of writing it: the number of overlapping copies in each stack equals the number of options in the bracket on the arrow before it (four aggregators, four circles; three scalers, three coloured stacks), so a reader counts the combinations straight off the circles.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year (2004.05718); venue NeurIPS recorded from the PDF first-page footer (venue_source: pdf). elements 'other' = the diagonally offset stacks of circles standing for sets of vectors. The output node repeats the centre node's teal, closing the figure on the same object it started from. A very low-ink figure: 24 circles (6 + 1 + 4 + 12 + 1), nine arrows and three arrow labels with two bracketed lists carry the whole method.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

insights.structure: One horizontal chain of four glyph groups joined by three labeled arrows: a star graph (pink neighbours around a teal center), a stack of purple circles, a three-color stack of circles, and a single teal output circle.
insights.data: Node features are circles; multiplicity of aggregators/scalers is drawn as stacked overlapping circle copies, and the operator lists (mean/max/min/std; identity/amplification/attenuation) are bracketed italic column vectors under the arrows.
insights.emphasis: Growth of the circle stacks (one, then four purple, then twelve in three colors) visually counts the aggregator x scaler combinations, which is the contribution.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right with labels above each arrow and the bracketed operator list beneath.
insights.avoid: The node colors (purple, red, blue) for the scaler groups are not explained, so a reader cannot tell which color means which scaler.

arrangement.units: no enclosures; four glyph groups separated by labeled arrows
